problem: A dark presentation has no resolvable colourway (gap G10: a dark mode theme). The system's reversed colourway — white on black — is an observed property of the source (docs/synthesis/dominion/00-evidence-inventory.md §1 and §6: the reversed version; gestalt 01-gestalt.md: 'Reversed colourway (white on black) exists and is recommended for large formats'; docs/synthesis/dominion/tile/tile.html: 'Reversed colourway — white on black, formal and large-format') and was composed by hand in cadence-dominion, but the pack neither declares it nor indexes it.
insufficiency: resolve('a dark mode theme') -> UNDEFINED; resolve('a dark theme') -> UNDEFINED; search('dark mode')/'theme' -> no hits. token-set/colour carries the palette roles but declares no reversed mapping and no vocabulary for it, so a consumer cannot reach the system's own inversion; each consumer decides the band/pewter/hairline mappings themselves — invention on a canon surface.
reuse_case: Themes recur across consumers; cadence-dominion shipped dark as 'the reversed colourway' (settings toggle, persisted), keeping red ceremonial-only and the blue focus glow intact. Declaring the mapping once keeps every consumer's inversion consistent instead of drifting per project.
composition_check: There is no compositional path: the reversed colourway is a property of the colour token-set itself (roles inverted), not something component/action, component/field or any recipe can express. The synthesis renders it (tile) but the pack neither declares nor indexes it, so a consumer can only compose it by reading the synthesis layer directly — exactly the de-facto coupling this proposal removes.

extend.declare: reversed colourway: ground black (#000); text, rules and structure white; band and pewter roles inverted; FIP red stays ceremonial-only (D-05); blue focus glow kept (D-21)
extend.note: The source recommends the reversal for large formats; applying it as a full UI ground is a declared, system-consistent interpretation — reviewers may modify or decline that step without affecting the declaration of the colourway itself.
